title: VERDICT: the documented self-host does not work. On an empty database instrumentation.ts exits 1 before creating a single table, and nothing in the running app ever writes the schema-meta row it demands
description: Static trace only (docker and psql are not installed on this machine, nothing was executed). Boot path for a container started against an empty Postgres: Dockerfile:114-115 ENTRYPOINT tini + CMD npm start -> next start -> instrumentation.ts register() (instrumentation.ts:28). At instrumentation.ts:91 it runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS vulnradar_schema_meta, at :99 it SELECTs the single row, and at :105 `if (metaRes.rows.length === 0)` it prints the SCHEMA VERSION NOT SET box and calls process.exit(1) at :144. The 2,900 lines of CREATE TABLE statements start at :279, after that gate, so they never run. A repo-wide grep for vulnradar_schema_meta finds exactly two writers: scripts/create-fresh-db/create-fresh-db.mjs:302 and scripts/migrate/_meta.mjs:69 (writeMeta). Neither is the app. The app never inserts that row under any code path, so the gate can never be satisfied by booting. The two commands the error box offers are also both dead ends on an empty DB: scripts/migrate/_detect.mjs:56 returns version:null when no fingerprint tables are present, and migrate.mjs:355 then aborts with "Could not detect a known schema version"; there is no empty-to-1.0.0 step in scripts/migrate/versions/. Only npm run db:create can bootstrap, and it is a side-by-side clone tool (scripts/create-fresh-db/create-fresh-db.mjs:6-18) that creates a DIFFERENTLY NAMED database ("default ends in _v3", :725) and reads its DDL from resolve(ROOT, "instrumentation.ts") (:69), so it needs the source checkout, not the image. docker-compose.yml:100 sets restart: unless-stopped, so the app container crash-loops forever. Four separate docs assert the opposite: README.md:79-82, app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:259-264 ("instrumentation.ts runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS for every table ... Look for Database schema verified successfully"), app/docs/setup/page.tsx:652-654, app/docs/config/page.tsx:1144-1147 ("Schema auto-creates on first boot; meta row is written on first scan via db:migrate"). The log line they tell the operator to look for exists at instrumentation.ts:3199, unreachable past the :144 exit.
impact: A new self-hoster who follows README.md exactly gets a Postgres container that comes up healthy and an app container that restart-loops with a red box telling them to run one of two commands, one of which cannot work on an empty database and the other of which is not present in the image (see host-02). There is no documented path from a fresh checkout plus a Postgres string to a running instance. This is the headline claim of the project's Self-Hosting section and it is false as written.
recommendation: In instrumentation.ts, split the metaRes.rows.length === 0 branch at :105 into two cases. If the public schema contains no application tables at all (query information_schema.tables for 'users'), treat it as a fresh install: fall through to the CREATE TABLE sequence at :279 and INSERT the meta row with schema_version = MIN_SCHEMA_VERSION at the end, next to the existing success log at :3199. Keep the current exit(1) only for the genuinely ambiguous case of a populated database with no meta row. Then correct README.md:78-82 and the three docs pages to describe whichever behaviour ships.

title: The Dockerfile runtime stage copies five paths and never copies scripts/, so db:create, db:migrate, the admin Backup button and the self-updater's migrate step are all unrunnable inside the published image
description: Static trace. The runner stage (Dockerfile:62) copies exactly five paths from the builder: public, .next, node_modules, package.json, next.config.mjs (Dockerfile:75-79). scripts/, instrumentation.ts and the rest of the source tree are not copied. Every npm script in package.json:29-40 resolves to node scripts/<something>.mjs, so inside the container all of them fail with a module-not-found on a path that does not exist. Concretely: (1) README.md:82 tells the operator to run `docker compose exec app npm run db:create`, which runs node scripts/create-fresh-db/create-fresh-db.mjs (package.json:31), absent; and because of host-01 the container is not even running, so `docker compose exec` fails first with a container-not-running error. (2) app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:545-548 tells the operator to run npm run db:migrate "inside the app container" after a schema change; same absence. (3) The admin panel Backup button, documented at app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:407-414 and promoted in .env.example's DATABASE BACKUPS block, goes POST /api/v3/admin/backup -> lib/backup/run-backup.ts:33, which spawns join(appRoot, "scripts", "backup-db.mjs"); absent, so the job always fails. (4) The self-updater runs npm run db:migrate -- --yes at lib/updater/apply.ts:353; absent. Dockerfile:88-92 installs postgresql-client specifically so that "scripts/migrate/migrate.mjs backs up the database to databases/ before applying any schema changes", a package installed for a script the image does not contain. AUDIT-013#deps-05 already noted a different Dockerfile comment describing something that does not exist; this is the same class of drift but with functional consequences.
impact: Every documented in-container maintenance operation fails: initialise the database, migrate after an upgrade, take a backup from the admin panel, and self-update. Combined with host-01 there is no way to recover a self-hosted instance from inside the container at all, and the operator must have a separate Node + source checkout with network access to the same Postgres.
recommendation: Add `COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/scripts ./scripts` and `COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/instrumentation.ts ./instrumentation.ts` to the runner stage after Dockerfile:79 (create-fresh-db.mjs:69 reads instrumentation.ts as its v3 schema source, so both are needed). Also copy lib/ if any script imports from it. Then re-verify that `docker compose exec app npm run db:create` resolves before README.md:82 is left pointing at it.

title: docker-compose.yml has no env_file, so 11 of the 48 environment variables the app reads are forwarded and the rest of .env is silently ignored, while the self-hosting docs state the app reads .env via env_file
description: Static analysis, measured with a Node script over `git ls-files` (48 distinct process.env.* names in app/, lib/, components/, scripts/, middleware.ts, instrumentation.ts, excluding NODE_ENV/PORT/HOSTNAME/NEXT_RUNTIME and test-only names). The app service at docker-compose.yml:52 declares only an `environment:` map (:55-72) and no `env_file:` key. Compose reads the project .env file for ${VAR} substitution INSIDE the compose file, but only the keys listed in that map are actually placed in the container's environment. The map forwards 11 app variables: DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_SSL, NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY, SMTP_HOST/PORT/USER/PASS/FROM, NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY, TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY (plus CONTACT_EMAIL and NODE_ENV). Not forwarded, despite all being documented in .env.example and read in source: AI_PROVIDER, AI_BASE_URL, AI_MODEL, AI_API_KEY (lib/ai/provider.ts), STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, AUTH_SECRET, DISCORD_CLIENT_ID/CLIENT_SECRET/BOT_TOKEN/GUILD_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET, GITHUB_CLIENT_ID/SECRET, TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDR, DATABASE_SSL_CA, AVATAR_STORAGE_DIR, BACKUP_DIR, BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY, BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS, BACKUP_OFFSITE_UPLOAD_URL, NVD_API_KEY, WEB_RISK_API_KEY, URLHAUS_AUTH_KEY, LOGO_URL, SUPPORT_EMAIL, DISABLE_CSP, SECURITY_ALLOW_NON_BROWSER_API, and the four NEXT_PUBLIC SEO/verification vars. app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:243-244 states flatly "The app reads .env via env_file", and the same page then instructs the operator to put AI_BASE_URL / AI_MODEL / AI_API_KEY in .env (:213-217) and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in .env followed by `docker compose restart app` (:372-377). Neither reaches the process. docker-compose.dev.yml:46-61 has the identical map and the identical gap. This is the mechanism behind AUDIT-012#obs-08's "Invalid signature" symptom: on the shipped compose the webhook secret cannot be set at all.
impact: A self-hoster who configures AI, Stripe, Discord/Google/GitHub OAuth, a trusted proxy CIDR, a custom backup directory or a threat-intel API key in .env exactly as the docs say gets no error and no effect. Features silently stay off, and the failure looks like a bug in the feature rather than in the plumbing. OAuth being unreachable also removes the only sign-in path that works without SMTP (see host-04).
recommendation: Add `env_file: [.env]` to the app service in both docker-compose.yml (after :54) and docker-compose.dev.yml, keeping the explicit `environment:` map for the values that are composed rather than passed through (DATABASE_URL, NODE_ENV). If passing the whole file is undesirable, extend the map to cover every key in .env.example and correct app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:243-244.

title: Without SMTP a self-hoster can create an account but can never log in: signup leaves email_verified_at NULL, the verification email throws in production, and login refuses unverified accounts
description: Static trace. lib/email/email.ts:81 builds the SMTP transport only when SMTP_HOST && SMTP_USER && SMTP_PASS are all set, otherwise `transporter` is null. sendEmail then logs a warning and, when process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production", returns successfully (:407-418); in production it throws `new Error("Email service not configured")` at :427. Both Dockerfile:106 and docker-compose.yml:56 set NODE_ENV=production, so the production branch is the one self-hosters hit. app/api/v3/auth/signup/route.ts:215-222 sends the verification email inside a background catch that only console.errors, so signup returns 200 and the user row is created with email_verified_at NULL (the signup INSERT never sets it; grep across app/api/v3/auth/ shows the only setters are the OAuth callback, the staff-invite route, and app/api/v3/auth/verify-email/route.ts:77, which needs the token from the email). app/api/v3/auth/login/route.ts:164 then blocks the login with `unverified: true`. app/api/v3/auth/resend-verification/route.ts calls the same sendEmail and throws the same way. The two escape hatches are both closed on the default compose: OAuth sign-in sets email_verified_at immediately but its credentials are not forwarded to the container (host-03), and there is no admin setting to disable verification (grep for REQUIRE_EMAIL/EMAIL_VERIFICATION over lib/config finds only CONFIG_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_HOURS, a TTL). Every doc labels SMTP optional: app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:185 "# Optional: SMTP", docker-compose.yml:62 "# SMTP (optional, for emails)", app/docs/config/page.tsx:1160 "(Optional) Configure SMTP". The First Admin User procedure at app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:268-284 tells the operator to sign up and then run one SQL statement (UPDATE users SET role = 'admin'), and omits the UPDATE users SET email_verified_at = NOW() that is actually required to log in at all.
impact: The most likely self-hoster profile, someone with a Postgres string and no mail server, reaches a working signup form, creates the account the docs tell them to create, and is then locked out with a message about an email that was never sent and cannot be resent. There is no in-app recovery. The instance is unusable and the cause is not discoverable from the UI.
recommendation: Either mark the account verified at signup when no SMTP transport is configured (check the same SMTP_HOST/USER/PASS triple lib/email/email.ts:81 uses and set email_verified_at = NOW() in the signup INSERT), or add an explicit setting that skips verification. At minimum, add `UPDATE users SET email_verified_at = NOW() WHERE email = '...';` alongside the role UPDATE at app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:280 and stop calling SMTP optional there and in docker-compose.yml:62.

title: The documented self-host upgrade path is a no-op: the app service declares no build context, so `git pull && docker compose build app && docker compose up -d` re-pulls the same pinned 3.0.0 image
description: Static analysis. The app service in docker-compose.yml:52-53 declares `image: ghcr.io/vulnradar/vulnradar:3.0.0` and no `build:` key, unlike docker-compose.dev.yml:40-44 which does. app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:535-541 documents the upgrade as `cd vulnradar.dev; git pull; docker compose build app; docker compose up -d`. With no build context, `docker compose build app` cannot build anything from the pulled source, and the subsequent `up -d` reconciles against the pinned image tag, so the freshly pulled source has no effect whatsoever on what runs. The same shape breaks README.md:78-79, which labels `docker compose up -d` as "# 3. Build and run" immediately after a `git clone` at :70: the clone is only used for .env and lib/config/config-values.ts edits, and config-values.ts is baked into the image at build time (README.md:95 "Edit and rebuild"), so those edits also never take effect on the prod compose path. app/docs/setup/page.tsx:607-613 makes the same promise, offering `git clone` as the "Or build from source locally" alternative to curling the compose file, when both branches land on the same non-building compose. This extends AUDIT-013#deps-06, which recorded the 3.0.0-vs-3.7.2 pin: the new part is that the documented mechanism for getting off that pinned version does not build and the fork-customisation workflow the README sells is unreachable from the shipped compose.
impact: A self-hoster who forks and rebrands the app per README.md:88-102 sees none of their config-values.ts edits, and an operator following the documented upgrade steps believes they have upgraded while still running the 3.0.0 image. Neither failure produces an error message.
recommendation: Give the app service in docker-compose.yml a `build:` section alongside `image:` (context ., dockerfile Dockerfile, args NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL) so `docker compose build app` works and `up -d` prefers the local build, or change app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:535-541 and README.md:78 to the pull-only path (`docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`) and point fork customisation at docker-compose.dev.yml explicitly.

title: NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL is inlined at build time and the published image is built without the build-arg, so every self-hosted instance renders vulnradar.dev in 15 client components regardless of the runtime env var
description: Static analysis. lib/config/constants.ts:191 is `export const APP_URL = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL || CONFIG_APP_URL;`, with CONFIG_APP_URL = "https://vulnradar.dev" (lib/config/config-values.ts:141). Next.js replaces NEXT_PUBLIC_* with a literal at build time in any module that reaches the client bundle. A scan of every "use client" file under app/, components/, lib/ and hooks/ finds 15 that reference APP_URL, including components/landing/landing-api-example.tsx, components/demo/demo-hero.tsx, components/scanner/footer.tsx, components/admin/features/mass-email-manager.tsx and ten /docs pages. Dockerfile:16 declares ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL and :32 forwards it to ENV, but .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml passes no build-args at all, so the published ghcr.io image, which is the image docker-compose.yml:53 pulls, has the fallback literal baked into those bundles. Setting NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL in docker-compose.yml:59 changes only server-side reads. The comment at lib/config/constants.ts:177-184 states "Self-hosters set NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL (see the Dockerfile's build ARG ...)" and lists the consumers as emails, sitemap.xml, robots.txt and canonical/OG tags, which is accurate for the server half but does not cover the 15 client files. .env.example:19 describes the variable as "Used in emails, redirects, and client-side code", which is the part that does not work on the prebuilt image.
impact: On a self-hosted deployment at scanner.example.com, the docs pages, API examples, demo hero and footer shown to that operator's own users all print https://vulnradar.dev, so copied curl commands and links point at the upstream SaaS rather than the operator's instance. For a rebranded GPL fork this is a functional and a branding failure, and it is invisible in the logs.
recommendation: Either pass `build-args: NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` in .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml and tell self-hosters that the prebuilt image is hard-coded to the upstream URL (so they must build locally), or make APP_URL runtime-resolvable for client code: expose it through a server-rendered value in the root layout or an existing runtime-config endpoint and have the 15 client components read that instead of the compile-time constant.

title: docker-compose.yml mounts no persistent volume for backups or uploads, and /app is root-owned while the process runs as uid 1001, so the app cannot even create the directories its own docs promise
description: Static analysis. The production compose declares one volume, postgres_data (:114-116), and the app service (:52-112) mounts none. Two directories the app writes to are therefore on the container's throwaway writable layer: BACKUP_DIR, which defaults to join(process.cwd(), "backups") in both app/api/v3/admin/backup/route.ts:27 and scripts/backup-db.mjs:184, and the legacy avatar directory join(process.cwd(), "data", "avatars") in lib/uploads/avatar-migration.ts:48. Neither exists in the image, and neither can be created at runtime: the runner stage sets WORKDIR /app as root (Dockerfile:68) before switching to USER nextjs (:102), and the COPY --chown flags at :76-79 only chown the copied children, so /app itself stays root:root and a uid-1001 process cannot mkdir inside it. scripts/backup-db.mjs:200 calls mkdir(backupDir, { recursive: true }) and would fail with EACCES. .env.example:49-51 explicitly warns "On a container this MUST be a persistent/mounted volume, otherwise every backup is lost on the next rebuild/redeploy", and app/docs/setup/page.tsx:684 documents `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d` as the update command, which recreates the container. docker-compose.dev.yml:62-66 does mount avatar_data_dev and its comment says "See docker-compose.yml's avatar_data volume comment", a comment and volume that do not exist in docker-compose.yml.
impact: Backups taken from the admin panel or by cron inside the container land nowhere durable, and would fail on the permission error before that. An operator who follows the .env.example advice has no volume to point BACKUP_DIR at, and BACKUP_DIR is not forwarded to the container anyway (host-03). The dev compose's cross-reference tells the next maintainer a comment exists that does not.
recommendation: Add `backup_data:/app/backups` and `avatar_data:/app/data/avatars` volumes to the app service in docker-compose.yml with matching top-level volume entries, and add `RUN mkdir -p /app/backups /app/data/avatars && chown -R nextjs:nodejs /app/backups /app/data` to the Dockerfile runner stage before USER nextjs at :102. Fix the dangling cross-reference in docker-compose.dev.yml:63.

title: The self-updater advertises itself as supported inside Docker but writes into a root-owned /app as uid 1001, runs a migrate script the image does not contain, and any success is discarded by the documented update command
description: Static trace. isUpdaterSupported() (lib/updater/environment.ts:8-17) returns unsupported only when process.env.VERCEL is set; there is no container detection, so both app/api/v3/admin/updater/status/route.ts:37 and .../apply/route.ts:56 report the updater available inside the official image and the admin UI offers it. runUpdateJob then sets appRoot = process.cwd() (lib/updater/apply.ts:206), which is /app, and calls copyTreeOverlay(sourceRoot, appRoot) at :261 to write the release's full source tree there. /app is root:root because WORKDIR /app runs as root at Dockerfile:68 and the process runs as USER nextjs (uid 1001) from :102, so creating new top-level entries such as /app/lib or /app/app fails with EACCES, while pre-existing chowned files such as /app/package.json and /app/next.config.mjs would be overwritten in place first (overwriting an existing file needs write on the file, not the directory). The job then fails with a raw permission error after package.json has already been replaced with the new release's copy while node_modules and .next are still the old build. Even if the copy succeeded, the npm-ci step at :325 and the `npm run db:migrate -- --yes` step at :353 run against a tree with no scripts/ (host-02), and the final log line at :369 asks the admin to run `npm run build` and restart, which in a container means the next `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d` (app/docs/setup/page.tsx:684) throws the whole writable layer away. AUDIT-013#cov-06 recorded that this pipeline has 0% test coverage and AUDIT-013#migrate-01 that the migrate step it invokes stamps 3.0.0 on a schema missing 11 tables; this finding is about the updater being reachable at all in the deployment shape where it cannot work.
impact: A self-hosting admin sees an in-app Update button, clicks it, and gets a half-applied file copy plus an opaque EACCES in the job log, with package.json now describing a version whose code is not installed. In the worst case they then follow the log's advice and restart, and the update silently disappears on the next image pull.
recommendation: Extend isUpdaterSupported() in lib/updater/environment.ts to detect a container (existence of /.dockerenv, or an explicit CONTAINER/VULNRADAR_UPDATER_DISABLED env var set in the Dockerfile) and return supported: false with a reason pointing at `docker compose pull`. If in-container updating is wanted instead, chown /app to nextjs:nodejs in the runner stage and ship scripts/ (host-02).

title: API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY is defaulted to an empty string in compose instead of being a required substitution, so a missing key produces a crash-looping container rather than a compose-time error naming the variable
description: Static analysis. lib/config/env.ts:19-26 requires API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY to be exactly 64 characters, and instrumentation.ts:33-35 calls validateEnv() as the first thing register() does, so an empty value throws before anything else. docker-compose.yml:61 passes it as `${API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY:-}`, which substitutes the empty string when the variable is absent from .env. Compare docker-compose.yml:23, where POSTGRES_PASSWORD uses `${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?Set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}` and compose refuses to start with a named error. The result of the inconsistency is that the one variable .env.example:27 ships blank by design (API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY= with no value) is also the one that fails latest and least legibly: `docker compose up -d` reports success, and the operator has to run `docker compose logs app` on a restart-looping container to find the zod message. The Dockerfile comment at :41-44 explains the deliberate decision not to set a build-time placeholder so operators must inject a real key, which is right, but the compose file then undoes the loud failure that decision was meant to produce.
impact: The single most commonly missed self-host variable produces a container that reports as started and then crash-loops, indistinguishable at the `docker compose ps` level from the empty-database crash-loop in host-01. The operator has to correlate two different failures from the same symptom.
recommendation: Change docker-compose.yml:61 and docker-compose.dev.yml:51 to `${API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY:?Set API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY in .env (64 hex chars: node -e \"console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('hex'))\")}` so the failure happens at compose parse time with the generation command in the message.

title: The Docker sections of the docs describe a smoke-test service, a DB_PORT binding and an env_file that the compose file does not have, and describe db:create two contradictory ways on two pages
description: Static comparison of the four self-host docs against docker-compose.yml. (1) app/docs/setup/page.tsx:570-571 and app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:241-242 both say the compose provisions "Postgres + app + healthcheck + smoke test"; there are two services in docker-compose.yml:12-112 and no smoke-test service. (2) app/docs/setup/page.tsx:631-633 tells the operator to set DB_PORT=5432 under a "# Ports" heading described as "Used by docker-compose.yml"; DB_PORT appears nowhere in either compose file and the postgres service publishes no ports at all, deliberately. (3) The env_file claim at app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:243-244 is covered in host-03. (4) db:create is described as the fresh-install initialiser in README.md:81-82 and as the recovery command in instrumentation.ts:127-128, but correctly as a side-by-side clone for testing an upgrade on a copy of production at app/docs/setup/page.tsx:731-745; the script's own header (scripts/create-fresh-db/create-fresh-db.mjs:3-18) agrees with the setup page. Related: AUDIT-009#migration-06 recorded that db:create and db:migrate cannot be driven non-interactively, which is a further reason README.md:82's one-liner would not work even with the script present.
impact: An operator comparing the docs against the shipped compose finds three things that are not there, which erodes trust in the rest of the page, and the two contradictory descriptions of db:create mean whichever page they read first determines whether they expect a fresh install or a clone.
recommendation: Delete the "smoke test" clause at app/docs/setup/page.tsx:571 and app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:242, drop DB_PORT from the setup page's env block at :633 or add a ports mapping to the postgres service, and make README.md:81-82 match the setup page's accurate description of db:create once host-01 and host-02 are resolved.

title: .dockerignore patterns are root-anchored, so nested .env files (marketing/.env exists in this tree), the .claude worktree copy, audits/ and databases/ all enter the build context for the documented local-build path
description: Static analysis. Docker matches .dockerignore patterns against the whole context-relative path using filepath.Match semantics, where * does not cross a /, and only ** crosses directories. So `.env`, `.env.*` and `.env*.local` at .dockerignore:4-6 exclude only root-level dotenv files, and `node_modules` at :1 excludes only the root node_modules. A directory listing of this working tree shows ./marketing/.env present, which is not matched by any pattern; .claude/ (which per the audit brief holds a full second checkout at .claude/worktrees/agent-ad8a7d09dcde23fcc/, including its own node_modules), audits/, databases/ (gitignored at .gitignore:12 and described there as holding real pre-migration database backups), and cli/ are not listed either. Dockerfile:27 is `COPY . .`, so all of that lands in the builder stage. It does NOT reach the published image: the runner stage copies only public, .next, node_modules, package.json and next.config.mjs (Dockerfile:75-79), so the final artifact is clean. The exposure is the build context transfer and the builder layer cache on whatever machine runs the documented `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d --build` (docker-compose.dev.yml:14).
impact: Local image builds copy hundreds of megabytes of irrelevant tree, including a second full checkout, into the daemon and the layer cache, slowing every build. A nested .env with real values sits in the builder layer, which is retained in the local build cache and would be pushed if anyone ever added a cache-export or a stage that copies more broadly. Real but bounded, because the shipped image is unaffected today.
recommendation: Change the patterns in .dockerignore to their recursive forms (`**/.env`, `**/.env.*`, `**/node_modules`) and add `.claude`, `audits`, `databases`, `marketing`, `coverage`, `graphify-out` and `docker-compose.dev.yml`. Keep the `!.env.example` re-include after the broadened dotenv rules.

title: Negative results for the next audit: root .env.local is correctly excluded from the image, the container runs non-root with a real healthcheck and shutdown handlers, and Stripe, AI, Turnstile and Browserbase all degrade gracefully when unset
description: Recorded so the next audit does not re-derive them. All static, nothing executed. (1) Secret leak into the image: root .env.local IS matched by both `.env.*` and `.env*.local` at .dockerignore:5-6 and never enters the context; `!.env.example` at :7 correctly re-includes only the template. The nested caveat is host-11. (2) The `*.md` exclusion at .dockerignore:9 is root-anchored and therefore does not strip the five generated AI knowledge files under lib/ai/, and the prebuild compilers (package.json:13) read .ts sources (scripts/compile-changelog-knowledge.mjs:26 reads lib/changelog/data.ts), so the build is not broken by it. (3) Non-root: Dockerfile:71-72 creates uid/gid 1001 and :102 switches to it before EXPOSE. (4) HEALTHCHECK at Dockerfile:99-100 and docker-compose.yml:87-99 both target /api/v3/health, which does a real pool.connect plus a schema-version and required-tables probe (app/api/v3/health/route.ts:88-116) rather than the GitHub-only /api/version, and the path is in lib/config/public-paths.ts:109 so middleware does not block the probe.
